title: Optimize: fix double-counting when caching + batching are both applicable in savings estimate v1
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Fixes an issue where estimated savings could be overstated when both caching and batching were applicable for the same route/model. Adds regression coverage to prevent >100% savings and ensures consistent attribution in the UI.
body:
Context: We found a double-counting bug in savings estimation v1 when both caching and batching recommendations are applicable to the same route/model/region. The previous implementation computed per-lever savings independently against the same baseline and then summed them, which can overstate total savings (in a few cases exceeding baseline cost and/or producing unrealistic monthly impact). This showed up in staging Suggestions for high-volume tenants and was also reported as week-over-week swings/confusion (SUP-19344) when caching eligibility toggled.

What changed: Update the estimator to compute total savings from a combined scenario rather than summing independent deltas. We still surface per-lever deltas for explanation, but we now calculate them sequentially and clamp attribution so total never exceeds baseline. Concretely, we apply caching first (since it changes effective compute/token via hit-rate), then apply batching improvements to the remaining uncached workload. We also add invariants: total_estimated_savings_usd <= baseline_cost_usd and savings_pct in [0, 1].

ADR alignment: This matches ADR-0275 guidance on avoiding double-counting and makes the composability rules explicit in code comments + links. Added a short note to the ADR reference block in-code describing ordering/attribution. No schema changes.

Testing: Adds regression tests covering (1) caching-only, (2) batching-only, (3) caching+batching together with realistic hit-rate distributions and latency headroom. Includes a golden test to ensure combined total does not equal naive sum and stays within bounds.

Risk/rollout: Low risk; computation-only change. Does not modify API shape. Verified against recent token metering baselines in dev + staging. After merge we should monitor Suggestions adoption metrics for sudden drops in estimated savings (expected for affected cases) and keep an eye on any tenants whose savings disappear due to clamping/insufficient data.

Refs: ENG-2410, ADR-0275 (Savings estimation contract), PRs #18657 (savings estimation v1), #18661 (risk fields).
commits: optimize/savings: compute combined scenario for caching+batching (no naive sum)
tests: add regression fixtures for caching+batching overlap
docs: link estimator logic to ADR-0275 in code comments
review_conversation: Jonas Weber: The fix looks good, but can we make the ordering explicit (caching then batching) and justify it somewhere? Also add a guard that total savings cannot exceed baseline.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added ordering rationale in attribution.ts header with ADR-0275 link. Also introduced invariants.ts with clamps + explicit assertion in tests.
Sana Farid: Can you confirm that sequential attribution won’t make per-lever numbers look inconsistent (i.e., caching savings changes batching savings)? We should avoid confusing explanations.

Nadia Rahman (author): Yes, batching is now calculated on the post-cache residual workload. Added a line in the explanation builder so the UI can show: "Batching savings estimated on remaining uncached requests" (no schema change; it’s part of rationale bullets).
Logan Wright: Any telemetry coupling here? If cache hit-rate is stale, does this make the estimates worse?
Nadia Rahman (author): No new telemetry requirements. Same hit-rate input; we’re just combining correctly. Staleness behavior unchanged (still handled upstream by freshness gating).
Hassan Mirza: Please add a test case where naive sum would exceed baseline (e.g., high cache hit + aggressive batching) to make the regression obvious.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added fixture caching_batching_overlap.json where naive sum produces 112% savings; combined scenario returns 63% and stays within bounds.
Jonas Weber: Approved after the regression fixture + invariants. Thanks.
